definitions.gloss: paper-thin difference; razor-thin margin; fine line
definitions.explanation: An extremely small difference between two things, especially between success and failure, genius and madness, or other opposing outcomes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{成功|せいこう}→成功：02638_seikou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ}だ。
examples.english: Success and failure are separated by a paper-thin margin.

examples.japanese: ⟦{天才|てんさい}→天才：09934_tensai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{狂気|きょうき}→狂気：27800_kyouki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われる→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It is said that genius and madness are separated by a fine line.

examples.japanese: {紙一重|かみひとえ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{差|さ}→差：02771_sa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{決勝|けっしょう}→決勝：04742_kesshou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{進|すす}む→進む：01225_susumu⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: I was able to advance to the finals by the slimmest of margins.

notes:
Literally "the thickness of one sheet of paper," used to describe an extremely small gap between two contrasting outcomes or qualities. Often used in set phrases comparing opposing concepts.

USAGE:
Most commonly appears in the pattern A⟦と→と：00512_to⟧B⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ} (A and B are paper-thin apart). Also used with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{差|さ}→差：02771_sa⟧ (difference) to describe narrow margins in competitions or decisions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紙一重|かみひとえ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{差|さ}→差：02771_sa⟧ — a razor-thin difference
- {紙一重|かみひとえ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{勝利|しょうり}→勝利：11795_shouri⟧ — a victory by the slimmest margin
- ⟦{成功|せいこう}→成功：02638_seikou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ} — success and failure are a hair's breadth apart
- ⟦{天才|てんさい}→天才：09934_tensai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{狂気|きょうき}→狂気：27800_kyouki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{紙一重|かみひとえ} — genius and madness are separated by a fine line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{僅差|きんさ}→僅差：11526_kinsa⟧ — narrow margin (more neutral, often for scores)
- {際|きわ}どい — close, narrow, borderline (adjective)
